text:
Raptors which have been observed include the great horned owl, saw-whet owl, golden eagle, sparrow hawk, prairie falcon, rough-legged hawk, red-tailed hawk, Swainson's hawk, and marsh hawk. Nesting of raptors has not been documented, although all of the observed species with the exception of the rough-legged hawk may nest in the area.
A variety of songbird species have been observed in the Project

Area. During the breeding and nesting seasons, the most abundant

species in grassland and sagebrush habitats are the western meadowlark,

lark sparrow and vesper sparrow. In the ponderosa pine habitat type,

the black-capped chickadee, red-breasted nuthatch, chipping sparrow,

red-headed woodpecker, flicker, mourning dove, house wren, western wood

pewee and robin are common during spring and summer months.

Amphibians and Reptiles - Leopard frogs (Rana pipiens) and painted

turtles (Chrysemys picta) have been commonly observed in aquatic habit
ats. A number of species of snakes may inhabit the area; only the racer

(Coluber constrictor) and prairie rattlesnake (Crotalus viridus viridis)

have been observed. Amphibians and reptiles which may occur in the area

are listed in Appendix F.
Aquatic Ecology - Tracts II and Tract III contribute run-off and spring snowmelt water to two drainages in the area: Tullock Creek and Sarpy Creek. The western portion of Tract II is drained by Cottonwood, East Cabin and Plum Creeks plus an unnamed drainage. The eastern portion of Tract II and all of Tract III is drained into Sarpy Creek and the East Fork of Sarpy Creek. Sarpy Creek, East Fork of Sarpy Creek and all their tributaries in the lease tracts are intermittent in nature. A total of 82 springs have been located within the boundaries of the Westmoreland lease.
